articles.title: Asus ROG Raikiri II Review - IGN
articles.body:
I’ve used hundreds of controllers, and while the recent string of ‘pro controllers’ with extra buttons and fancy RGB lighting have been interesting, none of them have really justified the extra price tag for me. But the Asus ROG Raikiri II is one of the few pro controllers that feels just as good as a regular Xbox Series X or PS5 gamepad – and without the added weight of Microsoft’s Elite controllers .

Because rather than iterating on some of the more bizarre design decisions of its predecessor, the Raikiri II basically takes the comfortable controller part of the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X and just, well, makes it into a full-blown controller. That makes it a natural companion for the handheld gaming PC for anyone that’s using it to play on a TV or gaming monitor , but even without the Ally, the Raikiri II is just a damn fine gamepad.

At first glance, the Asus ROG Raikiri II looks like pretty much any other third-party Xbox controller. However, look closer, and there are a few more face buttons than would otherwise be there. Just like the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X that came out last year, the Raikiri II has extra menu buttons, with one on the top left, next to the Xbox button, meant to bring up the Asus Armoury Crate software, and the library button on the other side that is meant to bring up the library tab of the Xbox full screen experience.

Here’s the catch, though: these buttons straight up don’t do anything on a standard gaming PC. Asus even has a piece of software that you can download to give the Raikiri II the same functionality as the controller on the Xbox Ally X, but in my testing it only works on, well, the Xbox Ally X. That’s great for anyone plugging their Xbox Ally X into their TV to play from the couch – you’re going to get the same functionality as in handheld mode. But if you’re buying this controller for your PC, you’re going to have two essentially useless buttons on the controller. But, hey, at least they don’t actually do anything when you accidentally hit them.

Aesthetically, the Asus ROG Raikiri II borrows a lot from Asus’ latest handheld, too. It has the same black colorway, and you can even look up close and it has the same tiny “ROG Xbox” lettering on the front of the peripheral.

And of course, being an import from the Republic of Gamers, this controller has plenty of RGB lighting. There are three zones of lighting, one in the middle, in the shape of the ROG logo, and then a stripe on either side of the controller. By default, the lighting has the standard blinking rainbow effect, but you can customize it using Asus’ Gear Link web portal. Asus isn’t the first company to move hardware management to a web app, but it is much better than having some heavy software always running in the background on your PC – at least if you have a stable internet connection.

The software does allow you to customize button assignments and even the response curve of your thumbsticks. However, the paddles on the back of the controller can only be assigned to one of the existing controller buttons. That is useful, especially if you’re playing a game that requires you to press buttons while you’re moving or something, but I would have liked to see some kind of macro support here. Just let me assign button combinations to the paddles – it would, for instance, make playing Final Fantasy XIV on a controller a bit easier.

Much like other ‘pro’ controllers like the Razer Wolverine V3 Pro , the Raikiri II does allow you to swap out the thumbsticks. There is an extra set of thumbsticks included in the box, but they’re very long.

The controller also comes with a charging stand, which wirelessly charges the controller via some POGO pins on the back. The stand fits nice and snug in the included carrying case with a hole in the back for the USB-C cable, much like the Xbox Elite Controller, but Asus also includes little feet that let you set it up wherever you want.

I’d actually recommend taking the stand out of the carrying case and setting it up somewhere near your gaming setup. The charging stand has a little USB port in the front of it, which you can use to connect the 2.4GHz dongle. Then, you can just place it somewhere out in the open, and you won’t have to worry about the signal from the dongle being interrupted by anything.

The Asus ROG Raikiri II is one of the few controllers out there right now that are using Tunneling Magnetoresistance, or TMR sensors. Just like Hall Effect, these sensors use magnets to more accurately track your inputs, they’re just a bit more power efficient. While it would have been enough to have these TMR sensors just in the analog sticks, the Raikiri II also has them in the triggers, which means both should stay accurate for years.

I obviously didn’t test this controller for years, just a couple of weeks, but even in that short time, I’ve been impressed by just how snappy this controller is. The analog sticks have this springiness to them that feels incredible – giving just enough resistance to feel like I’m moving something, without feeling like I’m fighting against them.

The triggers likewise feel incredibly accurate, especially when trying to drive around in Cyberpunk 2077, where the half-presses help me control the throttle of my car. You can also change the actuation point of the triggers with little switches on the back, but there are just two settings – all the way down and half-way. To this day, having a high-end controller stop the trigger press half-way down just feels weird, but it’s likely a boon for professional FPS players.

The face buttons, on the other hand, use micro switches, rather than TMR sensors, and they still feel incredibly responsive. However, the buttons are incredibly clicky, and they can get quite loud if you’re really mashing them. In the two weeks or so I’ve been using the controller, though, it hasn’t missed a click, so at least it’s reliable. And the micro switches will probably keep the buttons quick and responsive for quite a while.

It all comes together to a controller that just feels good to use. I’ll admit that I’m no esports pro, but even spending time in Assassin’s Creed: Shadows, I’ve noticed a difference just in how smooth the camera moves when I’m using the right analog stick. And unlike something like the Xbox Elite controller , it’s not too heavy, so it doesn’t start to weigh me down after a long gaming session.

And you’re going to be able to get some long gaming sessions out of this controller, too. Asus claims that the ROG Raikiri II will last up to 50 hours on a single charge. I’m not going to sit there for 50 hours straight to see if the controller meets those claims, but I have only run out of battery once in two weeks of very heavy usage.

The battery could potentially last even longer, too, but its sleep behavior is strange . After sitting idle for a while, the lighting will turn off, but the controller will stay on. There have been a couple of times where, out of instinct, I picked the controller up and went to hit the Xbox button to turn it back on, only for the Game Bar to pop up. Annoying, but that’s something I got used to after a few days.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Sonos Is Hosting Its Own Prime Day Sale With Up to 25% Off Soundbars, Subs and Speakers
articles.summary: You don't have to wait until Black Friday.
articles.body:
Sonos is joining in on the Amazon October Prime Day bonanza with its own sale. Jump start your holiday shopping with discounts up to 25% off Sonos' most popular soundbars, speakers, subwoofers, and headphones. The 25% markdown is about what I see for Black Friday, so chances are these deals are as good as the ones that will show up in November.

Sonos "Prime Day" Sale: Save Up to 25% Off

If you're looking for an easy solution to add great sound to your home, then you've probably already heard of Sonos. Sonos speakers are very easy to set up, don't take a large amount of space, and most importantly, offer distortion-free room-filling audio. They're definitely pricier than budget options, but the sound quality is comparable to speakers that cost hundreds more or take up much more space.

Sonos' flagship Arc Ultra soundbar drops to $899 after a $200 off discount. Given the number of upgrades, the Sonos Arc Ultra should be considered more as a new class of flagship soundbar than a mere update of the original Arc. Whereas the original Arc featured a 5.0.2ch setup with eleven speakers and no sub, the Arc Ultra boasts an expanded 9.4.1ch setup with fourteen speakers including a four-motor, dual-membrane Sound Motion woofer for better bass response and low end. This is a pretty significant upgrade alone especially if you don't plan on adding a discrete subwoofer.

The Sonos Sub 4 drops to $749 after a $150 off discount. The audio savvy knows that a single speaker isn't enough to reproduce an entire soundstage. If you could pick only one other speaker, then a subwoofer would make the most meaningful impact. The Sub 4 features dual inward-facing 5"x8" woofers and a ported design. Improvements over the Sub 3 include a faster processor, more RAM, and Wi-Fi 6 networking.

The Sonos Era 100 SL drops to $149 after a $40 off instant discount. The Era 100 is Sonos' most popular and most versatile speaker. The "SL" variant doesn't have a microphone, so you can't use it with a voice activated smart assistant. A common practice is to buy one Era 100 speaker and the rest Era 100 SL to save on cost.

Despite its compact size, the Era 100 houses two tweeters, a mid-woofer, and three class-D digital amplifiers to produce precise, distortion-free audio even at high volumes. It has a built-in microphone for smart functionality. Because of its flexibility, it's often paired with a sound bar or a second Era speaker.

$100 Off the Sonos Era 300 Smart Speaker

The Era 300 is down to $399 after a $100 off instant discount. It's nearly double the size and weight of an Era 100 and sounds better because of it. The Era 300 is also shaped differently, but there's a reason for that. The hourglass figure is designed to optimally arrange the six speakers so that they fire sound in all directions, enhancing Dolby Atmos and spatial audio effects. The Era 300 consist of four tweeters and two woofers paired with Class-D digital amplifiers and custom waveguides to help project sound to all corners of your room.

The Sonos Beam is a great option for someone who requires a more compact sound bar or simply doesn't want to spend $900 on the Arc Ultra. It's currently on sale for $359 after a $140 off instant discount. The Beam (Gen 2) is a 26-inch long, 5.0-channel soundbar with one tweeter and four mid-woofers for natural, balanced sound and four passive radiators to help with the low end. Although the Beam doesn't have physical height channels, it has two virtual height channels for Dolby Atmos support. It has a microphone for voice control.

$110 Off the Sonos Ace Noise Canceling Headphone

The Sonos Ace drops to the lowest price I've seen for a new, retail boxed set. It's currently $239 after a $110 off instant discount. This premium wireless headphone features Dolby Atmos spatial audio with dynamic head tracking, lossless audio streaming over Bluetooth, effective active noise cancellation thanks to eight optimally positioned microphones (plus Aware mode), custom designed 40mm dynamic drivers for accurate, distortion-free audio, a mix of plush memory foam and vegan leather for all-day comfort, and a stainless steel headband skeleton for durability. articles.title: Smashing an Egg. That’s It, That's the Game
articles.summary: New Steam indie game Crack is all about smashing open a giant egg.
articles.body:
Is cracking a giant egg open the new Call of Duty? No, but Crack is further proof new Steam indie games are currently operating on a creative plane the rest of us can only hope to understand. It's a co-op game featuring an enormous egg in a laboratory. Nobody knows where it came from. Nobody knows what’s inside it. You've got a pickaxe and instructions to smash it open.

Things get more complicated from there. Crack promises an “incremental adventure,” meaning you don’t just stand around whacking the world’s largest omelette precursor with said pickaxe until something interesting happens.

You begin with relatively sensible egg-cracking equipment like pickaxes and chisels before progressing to dynamite and, apparently, “other weird tools” scattered around the mysterious laboratory. You can build scaffolding, and there are secret rooms, and any broken shells can be turned into currency. Most ominously, according to the press release for the game, "The egg has secrets," and, "The egg reacts to you. Whatever you do to it, it responds."

Honestly, it's a lot of pressure on whatever is inside that egg. Let's all take a moment to reflect on the sad tale of Peter Molyneux's Curiosity: What's Inside the Cube? Which promised the person that got to its core a life-changing prize. That prize turned out to be a revenue share in Molyneux's game Godus, which, at least by 2017, hadn't made a profit, and so there was zero revenue to share.

Crack is just the latest wonderfully specific game that Steam seems uniquely capable of promoting: Somebody has one deeply silly idea, refuses to dilute it with anything resembling good sense, and somehow ends up making the premise more compelling by taking it completely seriously. It feels like we're currently in a golden age for weird ways to burn time; there's a game called Needle In A Haystack Simulator where, well, you can figure out the main mechanic, and tidying up games are keeping people (and by people, I mean me) entranced by shelf stacking. Sadly, I've yet to find a game solely dedicated to peeling the labels off beer bottles in dive bars.

Crack will be released on Steam on October 26, and you can wishlist it here.

articles.title: Xbox Elite Controller Series 3 Might Catch Up to Other Premium Controllers, According to Leak
articles.summary: It looks like Microsoft is getting ready to launch an updated version of the Xbox Elite Controller with some much-needed improvements.
articles.body:
The Xbox Elite Controller was my introduction to premium controllers, and while I still love the way it feels in my hand, it's simply fallen out of my rotation when I have access to controllers like the Steelseries Aeon Pro or the ROG Raikiri II. But, it looks like Microsoft is getting ready to launch an updated version with some much-needed improvements.

The leaks appeared on Reddit , based on configuration files found on Spectrum, the platform behind the Xbox Design Lab. Those files have since been taken down, but previously pointed to a controller that gives users the choice between Hall Effect and TMR (tunneling magnetoresistance) sticks, an audio scroll wheel and more paddle designs.

Xbox Elite Wireless Series 2 Controller Review

This isn't the first time the Xbox Elite Controller Series 3 has leaked. Back in August, a user posted pictures of a supposed prototype to Reddit . However, that leak didn't reveal much about how the controller worked, whereas this one purports to reveal the specs behind the rumored high-end controller.

With all of the supposed features in this latest leak, the new Xbox Elite Controller would go head-to-head with some of the best PC and Xbox controllers on the market, especially if it's a bit more durable. My current series 2 is in a state of disrepair where the thumbsticks don't click in anymore, and its missing an analog stick. The controller is also notorious for scattering into a dozen different pieces whenever you drop it, leading to the back paddles and the D-pad flying everywhere.

If Microsoft is able to keep the good parts of the Series 2, like its extremely long battery life and perfect weight, while also adding these leaked features, I could see the Elite Controller getting its crown back. At least, as long as it doesn't come with a higher price. After all, even a couple years after the Xbox Elite Series 2 launched, that controller will still set you back around $167 at the time of writing.

That price seemed worth it when the Series 2 first launched, but now that we have the $99 Steam Controller and the $129 Asus ROG Raikiri II , Microsoft has its work cut out for it in the high-end controller market.

articles.title: Wizards of the Coast Union Demands Company Stop Pushing Generative AI
articles.summary: The Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering teams at Wizards of the Coast have just announced they're unionizing, joining the Wizards of the Coast-CWA (UWOTC-CWA) union formed by the Arena team earlier this year. In a letter of demands, the union has urged Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast leaders to stop pushing generative AI.
articles.body:
The Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering teams at Wizards of the Coast have just announced they're unionizing, joining the Wizards of the Coast-CWA (UWOTC-CWA) union formed by the Arena team earlier this year. In a letter of demands, the union has urged Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast leaders to stop pushing generative AI.

The Arena team, behind the online version of Magic: The Gathering, unionized back in April, and after months, has won its union election . Now, on October 8, that union is expanding to adopt the Dungeons & Dragons team and Team X – the team behind Magic: The Gathering and Dual Masters. The Wizards of the Coast-CWA is giving the company until October 13 to voluntarily recognize the expanded unit. However, Wizards did not voluntarily recognize the union when it was just the Arena team, so this will probably be an uphill battle.

The new union shared a petition ahead of its recognition, with demands it's presenting to Wizards of the Coast and Hasbro. One of those demands is protection against the encroachment of AI, where it says, "Leadership, without regard for the desires of our teams, has pushed for adoption of LLMs and generative AI. This has to stop; our teams deserve a robust and enforceable AI policy that aligns with our goals and values."

Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft – Sample Pages

Similar to another demand letter published when the union was first formed in April, UWOTC-CWA is also demanding 'Full ownership of what we create outside of work.' Back then, the union's announcement letter said, "Currently, if an employee makes anything creative in their free time, with their own resources, Hasbro may claim ownership. What we do in our free time should not be dictated by the company; neither should what we make in our free time be owned by the company."

The new petition reiterates this, saying, "Wizards can currently claim ownership over any IP created by employees during their tenure at Wizards, including works that are fully unrelated to Wizards IP. What we make in our free time should belong to us, not the company."

Only time will tell if Hasbro voluntarily recognizes the union, especially now that the UWOTC-CWA has already won one election. If Hasbro doesn't recognize the union, it'll have to file with the NLRB and win another election.

articles.title: Aion 2's Character Creator Is Going Viral for Its Bust Size Options, or Lack Thereof
articles.summary: Aion 2, a free-to-play MMO action RPG, is going viral for its character creation settings — more specifically, for how busty you can make your female character.
articles.body:
Aion 2, a free-to-play MMO action RPG, is going viral for its character creation settings — more specifically, for how busty you can make your female character.

Some players sink hours into character creators before they start an RPG. They’re almost a game all on their own, and players have been known to spend inordinate amounts of time creating all manner of monstrosities using the various sliders available to them. (Check out the absolutely bonkers creations players made when Street Fighter 6 launched, for example.)

However, Aion 2’s character creator is providing customization of a different type, and it has sparked quite a debate within the broader gaming community.

If you’re on gaming twitter at all, you’ve probably seen gameplay footage of someone using Aion 2’s character creator — or, to put it bluntly, abusing the bust size slider to increase the size of their character’s bosom. You know, for science.

This viral clip has stirred up a conversation around the types of bodies we see in video games. Some players have noticed that there doesn’t seem to be an option to decrease your character’s breast size from the default setting, leading to claims of ‘small chest erasure’ and the game’s developers catering only to a specific type of preference.

“I'm sorry, but if you really ‘love boobs,’ you'd be okay with small boobs existing too, but [the] minimum size is [a] C cup?” one user wrote in a viral quote-tweet on X.

“The minimum is way too big, isn’t it?” another asked .

However, the broader reaction to this particular viral clip from Aion 2’s character creator has been humor; both English-speaking and Japanese players have found the bust customization feature quite funny, sparking endless jokes about how they’ll need a few hours before they “actually start the game.”

Whatever the case may be, it’s at least brought some eyes to Aion 2 . Released on October 5 from South Korean developers NC, the game is set in a conflict between two warring nations. articles.title: Insomniac Finally Lets Players Toggle Wolverine's Story-Related Scent Trails on and Off With a 'Hint' Button
articles.summary: In the latest patch for Marvel’s Wolverine, Insomniac has enabled the long-awaited option for players to choose whether or not they want to use the game’s visible scent trails.
articles.body:
In the latest patch for Marvel’s Wolverine , Insomniac has enabled the long-awaited option for players to choose whether or not they want to use the game’s visible scent trails by making it a togglable 'hint' option mapped to a button on their controller.

The update dropped on October 6 after months of complaints from critical players, who felt the scent trails were too hand-holdy and didn’t let them explore enough on their own.

On Twitter/X, Insomniac explained that their decision to make the scent trails optional was a direct result of community feedback. Now, players can choose whether or not they'd like the option to toggle them on or off by using a Hint button, which is mapped to R3 on the PlayStation 5 controller.

This also goes for other features like the visibility of audio cues and nightmare roots, allowing players to navigate the game's environment and come upon the Nightmare Cabin by themselves.

“Our latest update for Marvel’s #WolverinePS5 is live and adds a new ‘Hint’ toggle for story-related Scent trails based on community feedback!” Insomniac wrote . “With recent updates, you now have more control over the visibility of Scents, Audio Cues, and Nightmare Roots.”

Also included in this patch were fixes for “additional community-reported issues related to crashes and bugs.”

This latest update follows a similar change to scent trails that Insomniac made in late September, which gave players the option of turning off the scents for Whiskey Bottle scent trails, Material Crate Audio Clues, and Nightmare Door Roots. Prior to that, they toned down the scent trails' visibility to "make these visuals less intense" by reducing their overall opacity.

Insomniac has held true to its word of improving Wolverine as time goes by. On September 15, the developer issued a message to players, saying it was "actively engaged with our player community and gathering feedback to further refine the player experience."

These players have not been shy about sharing their feelings with Insomniac. Wolverine might be the developer's single most-debated game of all time, in large part due to elements like its scent trails and white paint that tell players where to go.

Even Wolverine's design was a hot topic of debate, with some feeling actor Liam McIntyre didn't fit the role of Marvel's iconic short king — but McIntyre said he wasn't fazed by the criticism at all, owing to his experience in taking on the mantle of Spartacus in the mid-2010s.

articles.title: 'This Needs to Change' — PlayStation Fan Gets PSN Account Hacked and Restored, Acknowledges Others May Not Be as Lucky
articles.summary: PlayStation fans are questioning the security of their PSN accounts as yet another prominent community member had their account hacked and stolen.
articles.body:
PlayStation fans are questioning the security of their PSN accounts as yet another prominent community member had their account hacked and stolen.

Over the weekend, a prominent member of the PlayStation community, known as RealRadec, claimed that his PSN account had been hacked . He noted that the hackers had changed his login info, including his email, effectively locking him out of his account. He also stated that the PlayStation support phone number (which is somewhat infamous for being unhelpful anyways) was offline, leaving him without anyone to contact for assistance.

The situation mirrored one that happened to noted PlayStation podcaster and ex-IGNer Colin Moriarty earlier this summer. Moriarty had his PSN account stolen from him during a livestream, prompting some panic. However, given Moriarty's status in the PlayStation community, he was able to raise a lot of noise and receive assistance from various connections at Sony. Moriarty confirmed during a stream on Monday that he lent that same assistance to Radec, as the two have collaborated on Moriarty's podcasting network, Last Stand Media.

This all led to Radec getting his account back, but he was quick to note that he may not have been as lucky if he didn't have a platform and connections.

"It would be foolish of me not to acknowledge that this was dealt with as quickly as possible because of the position I'm in," said Radec . "Not many people have that reach, and I am fully aware of that. This is a problem that has been brewing for a long time now at PlayStation. No one deserves to have their account stolen from them and lose access to all of their games, DLC, save data, trophies, etc. It's not right. This needs to change."

Over the last few years, various PlayStation users have reported being hacked. It has also been reported that accounts are being stolen and resold online for hundreds of dollars, allowing nefarious buyers the ability to take someone else's digital games, trophies, and data.

Moriarty reported in May that hackers can provide otherwise mundane information (dates of PSN transactions, names, birthdays, and email addresses) to PlayStation support to prove their identity and gain access to accounts. Moriarty's producer and co-host, Dustin Furman, stated at the time that someone they trusted was able to replicate this on two accounts to prove it was more than just a theory. They went on to state that this allows hackers the ability to circumvent security methods like two-factor authentication. IGN has reached out to Sony for comment on how it is combatting the situation.

It's an ongoing issue, and one that has resulted in a lot of fear as we head into an all-digital era of PlayStation. Sony confirmed that it will no longer produce physical games starting in 2028, meaning PS6 will likely be an all-digital console. If you don't have the alternative of protecting yourself with physical games, it could create a lot of issues unless PlayStation patches its security issues.

articles.title: Xbox has secured exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights
articles.summary: The streaming rights come in November, when Microsoft is opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming.
articles.body: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told employees that Microsoft is getting ready to do something around Grand Theft Auto VI that “no other platform holder is doing” during an employee all-hands this morning. According to sources familiar with Microsoft’s plans, Xbox has managed to land a deal for the exclusive game streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI. The deal will mean only Xbox Cloud Gaming can stream Grand Theft Auto VI to players at launch, but it’s not clear how long the agreement will be in place. Rockstar Games still hasn’t announced a PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI, so this deal will allow Xbox to market its Xbox Cloud Gaming service to PC players who would otherwise need an Xbox Series X / S or PS5 console. News of the streaming rights comes around a month after Microsoft announced some major changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming. From November, the same month Grand Theft Auto VI releases, Microsoft is limiting streaming hours to just 15 hours for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for Premium subscribers, and just five hours for Game Pass Essential. Microsoft is also opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming with a pay-as-you-go option next month, rather than being limited to Game Pass subscriptions. The pay-as-you-go option is perfectly timed for Grand Theft Auto VI, allowing those who don’t own an Xbox, or who primarily play from a phone, to stream the game by paying for a bundle of hours. During the Xbox all-hands, Sharma also told employees that Project Helix, the next generation of Xbox hardware, will be a “family of devices” and that Microsoft will partner with others on some of those devices. Sharma first called Helix a family of devices last month in an interview, after Microsoft and AMD announced a “strategic multi-year partnership” last year to work together on “a portfolio of devices,” including Microsoft’s next-generation Xbox console.

articles.title: Xbox Reportedly Secures Exclusive Cloud Streaming Rights to GTA 6, Could Make Game Playable on PC at Launch
articles.summary: Xbox has reportedly secured exclusive streaming rights to GTA 6, possibly making the game playable on PC at launch via the cloud.
articles.body:
Xbox has reportedly secured exclusive streaming rights to GTA 6 , possibly making the game playable on PC at launch via the cloud.

The Verge has reported that Xbox will be the exclusive place to stream GTA 6 via the cloud at launch, though that doesn't mean you will need an Xbox console. Xbox offers access to its cloud streaming service on a multitude of devices, including PC, smart TVs, and mobile devices. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reportedly told employees during a recent town hall meeting that the company was planning to do something related to GTA 6 that "no other platform holder is doing."

The deal will reportedly begin with the game's release in November, though it's unclear how long it will be in place. However, if true, this would mean that PC players would have the opportunity to play GTA 6 on their device through the cloud. Although it won't boast any of the performance options, modding, and other unique features native to a PC version, it is a serviceable workaround for those who don't want to wait until Rockstar releases a port.

Microsoft has made some major changes in recent weeks to the number of hours Game Pass subscribers can stream their games , but The Verge notes that pay-as-you-go plans are going to be introduced in November. This will, in theory, allow users who want to play the game without access to a console to pay for timed access to GTA 6 via streaming.

IGN has reached out to Rockstar Games and Xbox for comment on the matter. The deal is certainly interesting, as The Verge also recently reported that Xbox was concerned about pre-order numbers for GTA 6 on its platform. Xbox CSO Matthew Ball denied these claims and noted that the game was breaking records on the platform, saying it matched the platform's share of the console market.

PlayStation also secured marketing rights to GTA 6, leading to limited-edition GTA 6 DualSense controllers . Rockstar has also promoted the game by saying footage was captured in real time on PS5 hardware. The PS5 version of the game will also boast unique features, which has led to Rockstar marketing the game with branding that says it will "play best" on PS5 .

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

Xbox's new streaming deal appears to be its way of directly competing with PlayStation around GTA 6. Given it is exceptionally difficult to get a console right now and they cost a fortune, this may be a huge win for Xbox, so long as they can effectively get the word out to casual gamers.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima Acknowledges Fan-Made P.T. Port That Runs Natively on PC
articles.summary: Hideo Kojima has acknowledged a fan-made port of P.T. that allows the game to run natively on Windows, making it playable for a wide majority of users after it was relegated to PS4 hell.
articles.body:
Hideo Kojima has acknowledged a fan-made port of P.T. that allows the game to run natively on Windows, making it playable for a wide majority of users after it was relegated to PS4 hell.

P.T. released in August 2014. Standing for ‘Playable Teaser,’ it was exactly that — a short demo of what was supposed to be the next Silent Hill game helmed by Hideo Kojima and starring Norman Reedus.

Unfortunately, due to Kojima’s falling out with Konami, the title was scrapped and the demo wiped from the PlayStation store in 2015. And that’s a shame, because it’s one of the most terrifying games ever made.

Luckily, a dedicated fan has worked tirelessly to make P.T. playable for those who either deleted it from their PS4s or who never got a chance to play it before it got nuked. A modder by the name LoreanXavier has revived the famous horror title on PC, and he says it’s about 97% complete at the time of writing.

The modder explained that this port isn’t an emulator or a remake of the game from the ground up; on his official Discord server documenting the project, he explained that he is essentially “reverse-engineering” the executable of the PlayStation 4, using the game’s original assets, as well as C++ and Vulcan, to make a version of the title that plays on PC with a dedicated Windows program.

It’s a 1:1 version of P.T., with the “same house, original content and Lua scripts, loops, events, progression and ending puzzle.” It even includes the game’s voice-recognition section.

“I've played through it myself. The game hasn't been turned into a different story or a new set of puzzles. Rendering is implemented for PC, and remaining graphical differences are being addressed separately. Optional enhanced graphics can change its appearance without changing the base game,” he explained.

30 minutes of gameplay for LoreanXavier’s PC port is already available to view on YouTube, and fans are already begging him to make his code open-source in the event that his project gets copystriked when it eventually releases.

But what’s most exciting isn’t the fact that people will get to play P.T. sometime soon; it’s that Hideo Kojima himself retweeted an article from GameRant discussing the port, meaning that he’s not only aware of it, but seemingly endorses its existence.

“The GOAT himself acknowledged my port. I am speechless. Seeing Hideo Kojima notice something I’ve poured so much time and passion into genuinely means the world to me. Thank you so much,” LoreanXavier wrote on Twitter/X in response to Kojima's retweet.

Kojima is keenly aware of what his community gets up to online, and is almost constantly retweeting fan art of his games; and given that Silent Hills never got to see the light of day, it’s probably refreshing for P.T. to get a breath of new life after a decade of languishing in the ether.

Kojima's next horror game, OD , is still in development. With Hunter Schafer and Sophia Lillis starring, fans are more eager than ever to experience a fully-fledged horror title from the maker of a strikingly terrifying game like P.T., and some are even convinced that the two games are somehow related .

articles.title: Yoshinobu Yamamoto strikes out 10, out-duels Chris Sale as Dodgers take NLDS Game 3
articles.summary: Yoshinobu Yamamoto continued his postseason dominance with seven strong innings and the Dodgers homered twice in their best showing against Chris Sale this s...
articles.body:
Yoshinobu Yamamoto continued his postseason dominance with seven strong innings and the Dodgers homered twice in their best showing against Chris Sale this season, beating the Atlanta Braves 3-1 on Tuesday night in Game 3 of the National League Division Series at Truist Park.

Los Angeles leads the best-of-5 series, two games to one.

Yamamoto only allowed two singles in the first four innings, one of which was a bunt that he was quick to field, but lost his footing when trying to throw to first base, one of three plays in Game 3 in which a Dodgers fielder slipped on the Truist Field turf.

Trouble came for Yamamoto in the fifth inning, with two single to open the frame followed by a one-out, four-pitch walk to pinch-hitter Rowdy Tellez, in just his 14th major league plate appearance on the season. One ground out to first base brought in a run but another grounder ended the inning with only one run in, and the Dodgers still leading.

He needed only 98 pitches to finish off seven innings, with just that one run across, and tied a season high with 10 strikeouts, done three times during the regular season .

Ten strikeouts are a new postseason career high for Yamamoto, who authored the 20th double-digit strikeout game in Dodgers postseason history , and the first since Shohei Ohtani in Game 4 of the 2025 NLCS.

Yamamoto's last five postseason appearances have been on the road, and he's won all five of them. In the four starts, Yamamoto lasted at least six innings and allowed exactly one run in all four games. There was a rather famous eight-out, championship-clinching scoreless relief appearance on zero days rest last November as well. In those five games Yamamoto has allowed four total runs in 33 2/3 innings, with 32 strikeouts against only four walks.

Sale, even at age 37, is a tough customer to face, and his first six outs were all strikeouts, looking very much like the ace that allowed three runs in 16 innings in two regular season starts against the Dodgers this year. But in between those six strikeouts the Dodgers had two hits, plus another reached on an error.

Two more hits came in the third inning, plus a catcher's interference, but the Dodgers stranded the bases loaded. That meant six left on base in what was still a scoreless game to that point, but there were encouraging signs, including Sale needing 62 pitches to get through the first three frames. Freddie Freeman, who homered in Game 2 , hit a ball the other way with enough distance to get over the left field wall, but Mauricio Dubón robbed him of a two-run home run with a fantastic catch .

The Dodgers started to get the fruits of their labor in the fourth inning, which began with Andy Pages singling for his first hit of the postseason. Kiké Hernández, making his first start of the playoffs, deposited a changeup into the left field seats for the first two runs on the game.

Two batters after Hernández's 12th postseason home run for the Dodgers — and his 17th career postseason shot — Freeman left no doubt this time around, taking Sale out, well over the wall in right field for a three-run inning.

Finally getting runs across underscored the work already put in by the Dodgers in making Sale work, and that paid off further when his night was done after five innings and 93 pitches.

Ohtani batted fifth in Game 3 , the first time in his three years with the Dodgers he's batted anywhere but first or second. Manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani hitting that low — which spaced out lefties Freeman, Ohtani, and Kyle Tucker with two batters in between them — was more of a one-time deployment because he was facing left-hander Chris Sale.

"I don't think it's a pressure thing. I do think it's something where he wants to do more," Roberts said earlier Tuesday. "But in that same breath, I do think that there's going to be a couple big spots today where he's going to be at-bat."

Sure enough, Ohtani's first two trips to the plate came with two runners on base. He chased badly on a strikeout in the first inning, but reached on catcher's inference in the third. Ohtani didn't bat again with any one on base, but those four total runners on with him at the plate were his most in a game since August 28. Ohtani did walk in the eighth inning, but was stranded.

Miguel Rojas started for a second straight game against a left-handed starter, and was hitless in three at-bats. While batting in the eighth inning, Rojas felt something on a swing and left the game in the middle of the plate appearance with lower back pain, the Dodgers announced during the game. Rojas also had one of the aforementioned slips on the west Truist Park turf, loosing his footing in making the final out of the fifth inning on a ground out.

Tommy Edman completed the at-bat and popped out, then remained in the game at second base.

Home runs : Kiké Hernández (1), Freddie Freeman (2)

WP — Yoshinobu Yamamoto (1-0) : 7 IP, 4 hits, 1 run, 1 walk, 10 strikeouts

LP — Chris Sale (0-1) : 5 IP, 7 hits, 3 runs, 7 strikeouts

The Dodgers try to close out the series with Tyler Glasnow on the mound on Wednesday night in Game 4 ( 3:08 p.m. PT, FS1 ), while right-hander Tyler Mahle goes for the Braves.

articles.title: Yoshinobu Yamamoto outduels Chris Sale as Dodgers seize NLDS lead
articles.summary: The Dodgers are one win away from the NLCS, after prevailing in a titanic clash of two ace pitchers
articles.body:
ATLANTA –– Two superstar pitchers were on the mound.

Two teams' seasons were essentially hanging in the balance.

And in Game 3 of the National League Division Series, an all-time, old-fashioned, heavyweight October pitchers' duel came down to two no-doubt, home run swings.

With a 3-1 win on Tuesday night that represented a monumental step in their pursuit of a third-straight World Series, the Dodgers and Yoshinobu Yamamoto got the best of Chris Sale and the Atlanta Braves.

Sale gave up a pair of home runs in the top of the fourth inning , with Kiké Hernández launching a two-run blast to left and Freddie Freeman belting a solo shot to right-center.

Yamamoto made the lead stand up, spinning seven spectacular innings of one-run ball in his latest playoff gem.

And now, the Dodgers hold a two-games-to-one lead in this best-of-five series, needing just one more victory to advance with Tyler Glasnow lined up for Game 4 and Tarik Skubal on deck for a Game 5, if it gets there.

"We know we're in for a battle," veteran Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas said pregame.

Once again, as they've done so often in October over the last couple years, the Dodgers were unfazed by the challenge.

The night before Game 3's titanic pitching clash, Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates laid out the situation succinctly.

To go deep in the playoffs, he said, "you're gonna have to beat some really good pitchers … You're gonna have to face an ace."

That, of course, applied to both teams, with Yamamoto making his 2026 postseason debut after a 14-9, 2.53 ERA regular season.

Still, the left-handed Sale represented a unique challenge for the two-time defending champions, entering Tuesday off the back of a career-best 2.16 ERA this year (even better than his 2024 Cy Young campaign), two clutch performances in last week's wild-card round, and a five-hit shutout of the Dodgers the last time he faced them in August.

Hernández and Rojas were drawn into the starting lineup, replacing Max Muncy and Tommy Edman to give the club two extra right-handed bats. Banged-up slugger Shohei Ohtani was also dropped to the No. 5 spot in the batting order, the lowest he had hit since the 2020 season with the Angels.

"I just feel this gives us the best chance to beat the Braves today, and combat Sale," manager Dave Roberts explained pregame. "I feel good about it."

Indeed, the Dodgers had Sale under pressure early and often, putting runners in scoring position in each of their first three trips to the plate (including a bases-loaded opportunity in the third) while driving up his pitch count with stressful, laborious innings.

Still, those were nothing but moral victories initially, with Sale wiggling out of each threat to keep the game scoreless –– with the help of outfielder Mauricio Dubón robbing Freeman of a surefire two-run homer on a leaping, full-sprint effort at the short wall in left in the third.

An inning later, however, the Dodgers would finally break through.

In his latest bit of postseason heroics, it was Hernández who broke the deadlock from the No. 9 spot, getting a changeup from Sale that caught too much of the inside corner of the plate and sending it screaming out to left for a two-run homer.

It was the 17th home run of Hernández's illustrious playoff career. It was a drive he celebrated with a primal scream as he rounded first base. And it turned a tense Truist Park crowd silent, save for raucous reception coming from the visiting third-base dugout.

Two batters later, the Dodgers bench would be going wild again.

Making his first postseason appearance in Atlanta since leaving the Braves for the Dodgers as a free agent five years ago, Freeman made sure not to be robbed again.

He squared up an inside fastball from Sale and uncorked a towering 399-foot bomb, sending it safely over the brick wall in right-center to make it a 3-0 game.

Of Sale's 13 career playoff appearances, it was the first since his postseason debut in 2017 in which he had given up multiple home runs. And though the Dodgers have yet to score any way other than the long ball this series –– falling to 0-for-13 with runners in scoring position after another hitless showing in that category Tuesday –– Yamamoto made sure the two big flies would stand up.

Tapping back into his historically dominant form from last October, Yamamoto largely breezed through a four-hit, one-walk, 10-strikeout masterpiece, burying the Braves with a flurry of fastballs, curveballs and splitters in a 98-pitch effort.

He faced his only real trouble in the fifth, when he limited the Braves to just one run from a bases-loaded, one-out jam.

And by the time he turned things over to the bullpen –– where Tanner Scott and, in his return to closing duties, Edwin Díaz finished off the game –– he had already outlasted Sale (who departed after the fifth) and put the Dodgers on track to a pivotal Game 3 victory.

articles.title: Padres lose All-Star pitcher immediately before NLDS Game 3
articles.summary: The right-hander might miss Game 4 if the Padres win Game 3 in San Diego.
articles.body:
The San Diego Padres will have to stave off elimination against the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of their National League Division Series on Tuesday, Oct. 6 without closer Mason Miller.

The two-time All-Star was a last-minute subtraction from the Padres' roster when he was placed on the paternity list.

MLB announced it had approved the roster substitution at 5:47 p.m. Tuesday, 43 minutes before the scheduled first pitch of the game at Petco Park. Wandy Peralta will take Miller's place on the roster Tuesday — and possibly for Wednesday's Game 4 if the Padres win.

The Brewers lead the best-of-five series 2-0 and will try to close it out on the Padres' home turf.

Miller, who made his second career All-Star Game appearance in July, was the losing pitcher in Game 2 of the series in Milwaukee.

Trailing 3-2, Brewers loaded the bases against Miller in the ninth inning at American Family Field with two outs in the ninth inning. Jackson Chourio's single into center field lifted Milwaukee to a 4-3 victory — and put the Padres on the brink of elimination.

In order to force a Game 4, they will have to win a game without their best relief pitcher.

Remarkably, it's the second time a Padres pitcher has been placed on the paternity list in the series.

Starting pitcher Walker Buehler missed the beginning of the series, but effectively didn't cost the Padres with his absence because he wasn't scheduled to pitch during his absence.

Now, the Padres can only hope Miller's absence from the bullpen doesn't cost them, either.

articles.title: Yamamoto’s Gem Gives Dodgers Edge vs. Braves in NLDS
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto allowed only one run over seven innings as LA downed the Atlanta Braves 3-1 in Game 3 of the National League Divis...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto allowed only one run over seven innings as LA downed the Atlanta Braves 3-1 in Game 3 of the National League Division Series, a win that wins back home-field advantage for the Dodgers.

With a 2-1 lead in the series, the Dodgers could clinch a berth in the NL Championship Series with a win on Wednesday.

Despite a lot of discussion about the decision to save reigning World Series MVP Yamamoto for Game 3, he looked like a pitcher on a mission, throwing seven innings and allowing four hits and one walk against 10 strikeouts.

That one run he allowed came in the fifth inning, but it was a relative win considering it came with one out and the bases loaded.

It ultimately proved to be the Braves' best shot at catching up to the Dodgers, who benefited from a pair of home runs.

Who hit the best for the Dodgers in Game 3?

Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman was robbed of a home run earlier in the game, but third baseman Kiké Hernández hit a two-run blast to open the scoring in the fourth inning, driving in center fielder Andy Pages in the process.

Freeman then finally got that home run two batters after Hernández, a moment Braves fans surely hated to see from their former franchise star.

All of those runs came against Braves starter Chris Sale, who blanked the Dodgers in a pitching duel in August , coincidentally also against Yamamoto.

On Tuesday, though, the Dodgers were able to get hits and ultimately score on Sale, breathing new life into this team.

The Dodgers stay in Atlanta for Game 4 on Wednesday.

First pitch is set for 3 p.m. PT, with Tyler Glasnow (5-2, 3.53 ERA, 98 strikeouts) on the mound for the Boys in Blue.

The Braves are starting Tyler Mahle (7-10, 3.99 ERA, 137 strikeouts).

With a win, the Dodgers move on to face the winners of the series between the San Diego Padres and Milwaukee Brewers.

If the Dodgers lose, the series comes back for a winner-take-all Game 5 on Friday night at Dodger Stadium. That game is slated to begin at 5 p.m. PT.

articles.summary: SAN DIEGO (AP) — Padres closer Mason Miller went on the postseason paternity list Tuesday night with San Diego facing elimination in the NL Division Series.T...
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Padres closer Mason Miller went on the postseason paternity list Tuesday night with San Diego facing elimination in the NL Division Series.

The intimidating All-Star reliever will miss at least one game, the Padres announced about 45 minutes before the first pitch. Wandy Peralta replaced Miller on the 26-man playoff roster.

Miller was one of the best closers in the majors this season for the Padres. With a fastball that regularly touches 104 mph, Miller converted 38 of his 41 save opportunities and went 5-2 with a 0.90 WHIP and 129 strikeouts over just 70 innings.

But Miller also blew the save in the ninth inning of the Padres' 4-3 loss to the Brewers in Milwaukee last Sunday, putting San Diego in an 0-2 hole in the best-of-five series.

While attempting to finish a two-inning save, Miller issued three walks before Jackson Chourio delivered a two-out, two-strike, two-RBI single to win it on Miller's 40th pitch.

Peralta was left off the Padres' initial NLDS roster despite posting a 3.61 ERA during the regular season as a solid middle reliever.

Miller is the second Padres pitcher to go on the paternity list in this playoff series.

Walker Buehler missed the first two games in Milwaukee while on the list, but replacement Randy Vasquez also didn't pitch while San Diego lost two straight in Milwaukee. Buehler, who returned to the Padres on Monday, recorded the final outs of the 2024 World Series while earning his first major league save for the Los Angeles Dodgers.

articles.title: Ace Combat 8 Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos and Top Features
articles.summary: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve from developer Bandai Namco Aces is much more than meets the eye.
articles.body:
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve from developer Bandai Namco Aces is much more than meets the eye.

On first pass, it's a combat flight simulation. The ninth main game in the storied series, Ace Combat 8 is a follow-up to Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown from 2019. Simple enough.

But Ace Combat 8 is so much more. It's a summer blockbuster movie with unexpected story depth, some JRPG goodness and an overall immersive experience that reaches far, far beyond its face-value niche.

Tack on serious multiplayer depth for good measure, and Ace Combat 8 certainly boasts the potential to be one of the year's sleeper hits.

As a combat flight arcade-sim hybrid, much of Ace Combat 8's presentation is about sheer draw distances and letting players loose.

Mission accomplished here. There's a feat of immersion happening here, with Ace Combat 8 boasting expansive geography below the player. Cities scale impressively well the closer one gets to the ground and the draw distances are stunning.

Usually, a game's skybox is just really fancy window dressing to offer a sense of immersion and scale. Here, though, it's a playground to maneuver and battle, with almost shocking lighting and fog effects. Dynamic weather really brings it all together, with cloud cover serving as literal cover, among the many examples of these million-dollar war machines still relying on nature to grab an advantage.

Talk about immersive, too. The bombastic, expected sound design is here. But so are the fun little wrinkles, like enemy pilots proudly playing their hunting song over the open channels.

It's important to stress just how critical sound design is in a game like this, too. Players stuck in aircraft need that emotion conveyed over the airwaves. Here, there's stunning voice acting and overall decisions over the radio in the form of rallying cries, taunting from enemies, or even hearing those a player was supposed to defend perish.

North of 30 aircraft gets split into four categories and each controls in a pretty unique way. There's a simple control scheme that gives the game big pick-up-and-play potential, too.

Ace Combat 8 leans a little more modern than its predecessors by permitting players to damage enemies anywhere, rather than restricting them to only doing damage to weak points.

Pre-fight loadout management is a big deal, too. Beyond just picking an aircraft, details like weapons, parts and punchable stuff impact in-mission details like ammo count, special weapons, aircraft performance, etc.

Sheer mission variety is a boon too. We're talking standard protection missions, hitting land targets, fighting battleships, finding hidden airshapes in cloud cover, it goes on and on. Little wrinkles on top of that, like a jammed radar, varying weather and others, just make it all the better.

It's all great fun when put together. And it's not what casual players might expect. It's not just "shoot the red-boxed enemies until mission win" at all. A game in this space requires serious mission-by-mission care in terms of design and pacing and frankly, lots of video games in any genre could learn a thing or two from the master class put on here.

Set in the fictional universe of Strangereal, the player's silent protagonist gets shot down, saved and inherits a rather fictional mythical status as a beacon of hope that keeps morale high.

The backdrop is, understandably, war: The Republic of Sotoa invades the Federation of Central Usea for reasons and the narrative loops in all sorts of fun warfare things, from airships to mech-looking things and orbital strikes, to name a few.

That's simplifying things, of course. It's truly a gripping tale that, at least a little bit ironically, goes out of its way to be pretty anti-war in its messaging. Think, the goofy-serious combo of a Metal Gear game. Jan Cope is the mouthpiece for this. Get it, cope ? Maybe unintentional, but funny.

What happens matters, too, as non-player characters can die via the actions of the player. All told, especially as the campaign nears its ending arc, it's one of the actually more surprising, enjoyable and memorable stories of the entire year. Little non-combat moments like getting to know crewmates in the first-person certainly help.

On the multiplayer front, Ace Combat 8 probably gets a little more innovative and modern than some might expect. There are 100-player lobbies to hang out in via a customized pilot avatar.

There are also, for better or worse, loot crates and a battle pass with free and paid tiers.

Actual gameplay comes down to co-op or PvP. The former involves a squad of up to four players joining forces to tackle objectives. Highest score amongst the squads is the winner.

On the competitive side, the PvP permits additional points for destroying other players. There's an added intensity on top of the whole element of competitive PvP in the first place by some smart score multipliers for, well, PvP'ing via destroying players.

Ace Combat 8 also tacks on limited modes and events to keep players coming back. Fun little wrinkles like going against elite AI enemies are some of the first offerings, and it's going to be pretty interesting to see what else pops up during the game's lifecycle.

Overall, the game runs well even with the impressive draw distances and particle effects, etc. There's also a strong suite of options, including two control options that offer simplified or expert (using shoulder buttons for fine details like pitch).

Who had Ace Combat 8 delivering the best story mode of 2026? Go play the lottery.

It's a testament to the almost surreal audio design in the form of immersive radio work. But it's also a nod to the superb design decisions like out-of-cockpit moments with well-thought-out characters and an anime-manga style that doesn't take itself too seriously.

Would-be players, though, should take Ace Combat 8 very seriously. It's much more than it seems, tells a gripping tale, offers some unforgettable gameplay moments and is a feat of mission design with a long-term replayability factor.

Shock value has nothing to do with it, either: It doesn't get much more Game of the Year material than Ace Combat 8.

articles.title: Xbox secures exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights ahead of launch: All details
articles.summary: Microsoft’s Xbox has reportedly landed exclusive cloud streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), a move that could give PC gamers access to the
articles.body: Microsoft’s Xbox has reportedly landed exclusive cloud streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), a move that could give PC gamers access to the highly anticipated title at launch even though Rockstar Games has yet to announce a PC version. According to a report by The Verge, Xbox Cloud Gaming will be the only cloud service allowed to stream GTA 6 when the game launches. The duration of the reported exclusivity agreement remains unclear. The report said Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told employees during an all-hands meeting that Microsoft was preparing to do something around GTA 6 that “no other platform holder is doing.” Sources familiar with the company’s plans told The Verge that the comment referred to Xbox securing exclusive streaming rights for the game.A cloud route to PCThe biggest effect may be on PC players. Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, and The Verge said the deal lets Xbox pitch its cloud service to PC players who would otherwise need an Xbox Series X/S or a PS5. That means the game could be playable on PC in November through cloud streaming, though it would not be a native PC release.For anyone weighing a console purchase just for GTA 6, the deal could provide another way in. For Microsoft, it is a chance to promote Xbox Cloud Gaming on a title that is expected to dominate the holiday season.A counter to PlayStation's marketing pushGTA 6 is set to launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. PlayStation holds the marketing deal for the game. Many ads say it "plays best on PS5." The reported streaming exclusivity gives Xbox its own GTA 6 selling point after that PlayStation-led campaign.Timing: Streaming limits arrive in NovemberThe report lands as Xbox Cloud Gaming is about to change. The Verge reports that starting in November, monthly cloud gaming access will be capped at 15 hours for Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for Premium subscribers and five hours for Essential subscribers. Those limits could matter for a game as large as GTA 6, where long sessions are common.To offset the caps, players will be able to buy bundles of streaming hours without needing a Game Pass subscription. articles.title: Apple TV's Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 4 Review — Slough House Is Down Yet Another Agent as the Season's Big Conspiracy Gets Even More Complicated
articles.summary: Slow Horses gets a little too tangled up in its own plot in a head-spinning but nonetheless exciting Episode 4.
articles.body:
This review contains full spoilers for Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 4, which is streaming on Apple TV now.

Slow Horses has added a tad too much starch to its plot-thickening slurry in Season 6’s fourth episode, “Lost and Found.” It’s hardly devoid of standout moments — the entire opening sequence in the neon-hued bowling alley, Frank Harkness and Jackson Lamb (Hugo Weaving and Gary Oldman, finally getting some meaty shared screentime) facing off in the Shake Shack, JK Coe’s (Tom Brooke) bathroom knife fight to the death against Jim (Kyle Soller) — but it’s reached the point in its short six-episode season where Slow Horses feels like it’s scrambling a bit to make sense of its, as MI5 overseer Oliver (Lucian Msamati) put it last episode, “petri dish of intrigue.”

Let’s put it under a microscope and unscramble where we’re at. Frank — who gets a taste of what it’s like to be Lamb, managing two spacey morons — is working for the scuzzy right-wing TV magnate Damien Cantor (Harry Lloyd). We already knew this from their meet-up in Episode 2 where Damien authorized Frank to kill Reece Nesmith (Lenny), but now there’s a twinge more clarity surrounding their circumstances. Damien wants some sort of contract from the Russians, and to prove his value, he was the one who had the dead Dog Andy Nesmith steal the Slough House file at the Park. But Damien wasn’t the one who directed anyone to start killing Slow Horses from that list; he just contracted Frank as the clean-up crew to cover the tracks of the document theft.

We can infer with a high degree of certainty, then, that Damien handed that list over to his Russian contact, who fed it to (or is working for) the GRU, Russia’s intelligence agency. And the GRU used the list to retaliate, sending in Jim and Jane (MyAnna Buring), against Diana Taverner’s retaliation for the recent nerve agent attacks that she’s attempting to re-cover up after the slip-up during her TV interview. For MI5’s assassination in Kazan, Russia, made to seem like a botched robbery, River (Jack Lowden) thinks that Diana (Kristin Scott Thomas) stole Sid Baker’s (Oliva Cooke) identity to make her look responsible on paper, which would explain why the murder duo would be out to get her. (But also: What if it actually was Sid? We still don’t really know for certain where she’s been hiding, other than vague allusions to a village where Diana apparently would visit.)

Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 4 — Images

Diana continues to be not innocent amid all of this in astounding new ways: She picks up the phone call that Damien threatened her with. Vassily Rasnokov, her equivalent in the GRU, is the voice on the other line, and the two intelligence service heads barter over the murders of their agents. Diana agrees that Vassily’s assassins can take out Sid if they agree to stop killing off the rest of the people in Slough House. (And why were all of them targeted anyway?) Diana selling Sid out is an even bigger gut-punch considering Sid has been obsessing over checking in with her, despite River telling Sid she should not trust Diana. River turns out to be right for once as Sid is kidnapped at gunpoint by Jim and Jane at the end of the episode.

Phew, what a mess! Everyone seems to be tied up with the Russians in some way. And this isn’t even getting into Reece’s attempt at blackmailing Frank, the crew of ladies who make it to the safe house that happens to also appear to be Diana’s holiday home (where Standish finds the wine cave…), and Coe’s bummer of a death. Poor Coe, left with his belly sliced open in a bathroom. At least he died as close as a Slow Horse can get to a hero’s death in confronting Jim after saving his colleagues’ asses numerous times this season. That all of these major developments happened in this single episode is also my biggest problem with it. I have no problem breaking out the proverbial cork board to piece together complicated storylines, but all of this plot in one go comes off as ill-paced, especially after a super-solid previous episode.

articles.summary: Why settle for just a TV when you can get the entire home theater.
articles.body:
Looking for a good deal on an LG OLED TV for Prime Day ? Well you are in luck because a good one finally went live. For a very limited time, Amazon is offering a new-for-2026 65" LG B6 4K OLED Smart TV for just $999.99 with free delivery after a $300 off discount that's automatically applied during checkout. But that's not all. Add the LG S30A 2.1ch soundbar and subwoofer bundle to your same cart and you'll get it for free .

65" LG B6 4K OLED TV (2026) for Under $1K Plus Free Soundbar

LG S30A 2.1ch Soundbar with Wireless Subwoofer

The B6 is LG's most affordable OLED TV for 2026. It's equipped with a newer generation W-OLED panel and an updated Alpha 8 AI Gen3 processor. Image quality is far superior to most non-OLED TVs thanks to its near-infinite contrast ratio, near-instantaneous response times, and ability to produce true blacks.

OLED TVs are also considered the best TVs for gaming and the B6 is no exception. It has a native 120Hz panel and four HDMI 2.1 ports, which means it can run games in 4K at up to 120fps on the PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X console. The LG B5 also supports variable refresh rate (VRR) up to 144Hz and auto low latency mode (ALLM).

Is the LG B6 OLED TV a good TV for the Nintendo Switch 2?

Despite being a current generation console, the Nintendo Switch 2 has lax TV requirements compared to the PS5 or Xbox Series X. When the Switch is connected to its dock and a television, it is only capable of outputting a 4K resolution signal at up to 60 frames per second. Oddly, it doesn’t even get VRR when docked – that’s reserved for handheld mode only. All that aside, the Switch 2 will still benefit from an OLED TV's overall image quality, just like how the Switch OLED looks better than the original Switch, despite the fact that the screens share similar specs.

articles.title: Brewers’ Pat Murphy shares eye-opening take after falling short in Game 3 vs. Padres
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers did almost everything right at the plate in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday night except the one thing that ma...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers did almost everything right at the plate in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday night except the one thing that mattered most. They outhit the San Diego Padres 11-6, drew four walks and kept traffic on the bases, yet still walked out of Petco Park with a 4-3 loss .

Manager Pat Murphy did not hide from what went wrong, but he also gave credit to the team across the field.

"We hit four or five balls over 100 that were caught, but we also punched out in big situations," Murphy said. "We had bases loaded. We had other big situations that we didn't cut through, so it's part of baseball. You're facing a good team with a good pitching staff."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The numbers back him up. Milwaukee left 11 runners on base, and one of its best late chances ended with a strikeout with the bases loaded. Christian Yelich also lined a ball up the middle in a big spot, only for Xander Bogaerts to snag it on a short hop and turn it into an out.

San Diego jumped ahead 2-0 in the third inning on a Fernando Tatis Jr. groundout and a Manny Machado RBI single. William Contreras answered with a solo homer in the fourth, and Jackson Chourio tied it with a sacrifice fly in the fifth. Jake Cronenworth put the Padres back in front with a solo shot in the bottom half, and a throwing error by Cooper Pratt in the sixth pushed the lead to 4-2 .

The Brewers got one back in the eighth but could not find the tying run. Michael King, who had thrown five innings just two days earlier, covered the final two frames for his first save since 2023 . San Diego needed him after closer Mason Miller was placed on the paternity list about 45 minutes before first pitch.

The loss also extended Milwaukee's postseason road losing streak to 12 games, a stat the Brewers will be eager to put to rest.

Milwaukee still leads the best-of-five series 2-1 and gets another crack at clinching in Game 4 on Wednesday at Petco Park. If the Padres force a decisive Game 5, the series would return to Milwaukee on Friday.

articles.title: Fishers native enters free agency after broken fibula. Will Fever bring 'big piece' back?
articles.summary: Fever guard Tyasha Harris was key for Indiana. Then she suffered an injury, and had a pivotal role in Raven Johnson’s ascent. What’s next for the free agent?
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — Tyasha Harris played a pivotal role for the Indiana Fever as their backup point guard during the 2026 WNBA season. Then she got injured and had a pivotal role in Raven Johnson 's playoff ascent. Now she's a free agent.

Fever coach Stephanie White provided insight into Harris' future during exit interviews Saturday.

"(I) don't have a status update," White said. "I know she has had successful surgery, and right now we're just checking in on her, making sure that she's feeling good and feeling OK."

Harris was ruled out for the season with a broken left fibula a day before Indiana's 105-82 Game 1 loss to the Las Vegas Aces on Sept. 27.

"It's heartbreaking," White said on Sept. 27. "Certainly, an emotional locker room after the game. Ty means a lot to us as a human being, and she means a lot to us as a player, too. I hate it for her because she worked so hard to get back. We're going to be with her through all of it."

Indiana Fever fans gather at Caitlin Clark’s shoe launch event at Nike store

The Fishers native signed with the Fever on a one-year, $400,000 deal for the 2026 season. She played five games in 2025 due to a left knee injury. Harris averaged 4.1 points and 2.0 assists per game in 2026. She stepped up for the Fever when needed. Harris started for an injured Caitlin Clark against the Los Angeles Sparks on June 27 and dropped 16 points. She went 5-for-5 from beyond the arc and scored 15 points on Aug. 14 against the Dallas Wings .

White added Harris was a "big part of what (we) do" and called her a floor general. She said Harris settled the team and praised her ability to hit shots. All-Star guard Kelsey Mitchell called Harris a "big piece" in the locker room.

Johnson handled primary backup point guard responsibilities during the playoffs. The rookie guard averaged 7.3 points in 21 minutes per game against the Aces. She posted 14 points on 6-of-7 shooting in Game 1.

"It felt like a regular game, just with more intensity and more physicality. The room for margin of error is very small, but it feels like college," Johnson told IndyStar. "I'm used to the bright lights. So there wasn't any pressure."

Harris, who also played for South Carolina in college, texted Johnson on Sunday morning to encourage her. Though Johnson was "ready for the moment," Johnson said she wanted to "play hard" for Harris.

White and Fever general manager Amber Cox stressed the need for frontcourt depth and a better defensive team next season. Harris contributes to the latter. But only time will tell if the Fever's desperation for a big will impact Harris' return.
